why_it_matters: Databases, deployment and sandboxes that an agent can provision in one call are where B2A revenue is already visible.
open_problem: The economics and security of short-lived resources that agents create, and dependence on a few coding agents.
standards: MCP serves as the provisioning interface.
companies: Supabase; Neon; Vercel; Cloudflare Workers; Daytona; E2B; Modal

why_it_matters: Every site now has to tell a customer's agent from an attacker's, and blocking both loses sales.
open_problem: Good and bad agents automate the same way. Up to 34% of the data fraud models rely on was missing in one in-chat checkout.
standards: None of its own. Depends on Web Bot Auth and network agent tokens.
companies: HUMAN Security; DataDome; Kasada; Cloudflare; Riskified; Forter

why_it_matters: Companies will not let agents spend or act for them without a record of what they did and why.
open_problem: Evaluating multi-step agents in production and proving compliance.
standards: MCP's 2026 roadmap prioritises audit trails, single sign-on and gateways.

why_it_matters: An agent can only buy what it can read. Structured product data is the new shelf space.
open_problem: Merchant data quality and slow merchant uptake of the new tools.
standards: The ACP and UCP specifications for feeds and checkout.
companies: Shopify; Google; Walmart; Stripe; Parallel Web Systems

why_it_matters: Being the product a model recommends, then being the one an agent can evaluate and buy, replaces ranking on a results page.
open_problem: Proving what changes a model's answer and whether it converts.
standards: None. llms.txt is on 36,120 sites but 97% of those files are never requested.

why_it_matters: Agents need to call, text and email businesses and each other. Voice is the first channel to scale.
open_problem: Authentication, spam and consent when agents contact agents.

technology: Network and edge for agent traffic
why_it_matters: The edge is where agent traffic is identified, shaped and, increasingly, charged for.
open_problem: Charging for agent traffic. Pay-per-crawl revenue is still undisclosed.
companies: Cloudflare; Akamai; Fastly; Cisco; Nokia; Ericsson

why_it_matters: An agent cannot be a customer until it can pay. Card networks, Stripe and stablecoin rails are all building for it.
open_problem: Who pays when an agent buys the wrong thing. There is no network dispute rule, and volumes are tiny or undisclosed.
standards: Visa and OpenAI aligned their protocols in June 2026. The x402 Foundation launched under the Linux Foundation in July 2026.
companies: Visa; Mastercard; Stripe; Coinbase; American Express; Natural; Catena Labs

why_it_matters: A business needs to know which agent is at the door, who it acts for and what it is allowed to do.
open_problem: Binding an agent to a person and a scoped mandate in a way every vendor accepts.
standards: Web Bot Auth is an IETF working-group draft on the standards track, dated October 2026. It is not yet an RFC.
companies: Cloudflare; Google; Visa; Keycard; Descope; Okta

why_it_matters: MCP is already the default way agents reach tools. The commerce protocols that let them buy are a year or two behind.
open_problem: Rival commerce protocols (ACP, UCP, card-network schemes) and MCP security, with more than 30 CVEs in early 2026.
standards: MCP and A2A sit under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. UCP launched in January 2026.
companies: Anthropic; OpenAI; Google; Microsoft; Stripe; Shopify

why_it_matters: The article's app store for agents: where an agent finds a tool decides who gets the business.
open_problem: The assistant's owner controls distribution, and under 5% of public MCP servers are monetised.

why_it_matters: Browser use is how most agent traffic arrives today, and it works on any site without integration.
open_problem: Prompt injection, and the legal right of an agent to access a site at all.
standards: None. Relies on Web Bot Auth for identification.
companies: Meta; Perplexity; Anthropic; Google; OpenAI; Browserbase

why_it_matters: An agent that knows a user's preferences and history buys better, and whoever holds that context holds the customer.
open_problem: Moving a user's context between assistants, and privacy.

why_it_matters: Phone makers can put an agent in front of billions of people with the personal data already on the device.
open_problem: A capability gap against cloud models, and regulatory access rules. Apple withheld its assistant from the EU at launch.

why_it_matters: When both buyer and seller are agents, price lists, discounts and terms have to be published for machines and negotiated by them.
open_problem: No shared format for terms, discounts or an agent's authority to commit. No dedicated funding found.
standards: x402, which revives the HTTP 402 status code, is the only live standard for signalling a price.
